head: f5f68bc435042afd52114e7e2363d4f2575b8014
summary: Fail. The draft adds a careful but disabled guarded post-merge close design. The core outcome of issue #115, verified automatic closure after a real asynchronous native merge, is not delivered. recovery_entry.verify_rollout always raises recovery_rollout_not_verified. Every guarded path calls it first: the recovery entry, the guarded native writer, adoption_guard.begin and the target-review preflight. No recovery workflow is deployed. The unguarded writer only prints checkpoint records, and nothing consumes them. There is no hosted asynchronous merge-and-close proof; the only real-provider evidence is the Core #77 fixture, which shows a manual close. The controlled hosted issues:write comparison was not performed. The human-listed gaps remain open: actor and launcher adoption, request ownership and cancellation, and recovery before the first status. One new liveness bug: in guarded mode, block_unadmitted runs on every later wake for a PR whose guard is held by the run that queued it. It replaces that PR's success status with pending. Because the request owner keeps the guard and no later run can acquire it or re-verify the PR, the strict required status can block the queued merge indefinitely. Hosted controls passed 825 synthetic tests, but that is not hosted closure proof.

findings.title: Verified issue closure is never reachable
findings.detail: verify_rollout always raises recovery_rollout_not_verified, and every guarded entry point calls it before writing. No recovery workflow is deployed, and nothing consumes the unguarded checkpoint records. A linked issue still stays open after an asynchronous native merge unless a human closes it.
findings.required_fix: Implement and review rollout evidence verification, deploy the recovery path through reviewed policy adoption, and demonstrate automatic closure.

findings.title: A queued PR can be blocked indefinitely by block_unadmitted under its own retained guard
findings.detail: In guarded reconcile, a PR queued by run A keeps A's merge guard because settle and cancel_blocked retain the guard while a request exists. On any later wake, guarded.begin fails for that PR, and block_unadmitted sees the newest Actions status is success and posts pending. No later run can acquire the guard to re-verify and publish success, and the request is never cancelled. The strict required status therefore blocks the queued merge indefinitely. Wakes from the worker's finish dispatch, the recovery dispatch and issue events make this likely.
findings.required_fix: Let the original guard owner re-verify and re-publish success for its queued PR, or bind request provenance to the guard so a later run can take over or cancel safely. Add a control covering a queued PR followed by a later wake.

findings.title: No real hosted asynchronous merge and automatic close proof
findings.detail: The issue requires verifying actual cloud behaviour before claiming automatic closure. The only real-provider evidence is the Core #77 fixture, which shows a manual close.
findings.required_fix: Run and record a controlled hosted asynchronous native merge in which the mechanism closes the linked issue, plus hosted negative controls.

findings.title: issues:write permission hypothesis not tested
findings.detail: The issue requires a controlled hosted comparison before changing a production permission or treating native auto-close as reliable. No comparison is recorded.
findings.required_fix: Perform and document a controlled hosted comparison, keeping the exact CI, review and ownership gates.

findings.title: Actor and launcher adoption, request ownership and pre-status recovery are unimplemented
findings.detail: cancel_blocked always retains a queued request because its provenance cannot be bound to a run. Cancellation and its race with merging are unimplemented. An admission interrupted before the first status has no durable pending-write recovery. rollout_inventory cannot prove that launchers have stopped.
findings.required_fix: Bind native request provenance to the guard, implement safe cancellation and pre-status crash recovery, and provide verified actor and launcher adoption evidence.
